gap: No result ChatGPT got says that the makers' headline battery figures assume the backlight is off. With the lights on, the full-height Keychron Q1 Max is rated for only about 30 h, at its lowest RGB brightness (it claims up to 180 h unlit), and the low-profile NuPhy Air75 V2 is rated for 35–57 h (it claims up to 220 h unlit). That is a cut of roughly 4 to 6 times that neither headline shows.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no search in either saved chat and got no results. Nothing was cited, so there are no rival pages to compare against. Its answer states only general traits such as 'shorter travel', 'portability' and 'customization', with no figures. It gives no battery life, height or travel numbers and never says what conditions makers measure them under. Any sourced, like-for-like figure is new against what the shopper saw.
decides: It doesn't change the pick between low-profile and full-height, but it corrects a hidden assumption. ChatGPT named the Q1 Max and the Air75 V2. Their headline battery claims (180 h and 220 h) are both lights-off figures. Measured the same way, with the backlight on, the 4,000 mAh in each lasts about one to two working weeks, not a month or more. The full-height Q1 Max is also 22.6 mm tall at the front and 35.8 mm at the back before keycaps, by KitGuru's figures. That supports ChatGPT's ergonomic point: a full-height board like this will likely need a wrist rest.

findings.note: Greenkeys reproduces NuPhy's official spec: 'Working Time (all lights on): 35~57 hours (lab test result)' and 'all lights off: Up to 220 hours'. 220/57 ≈ 3.9× and 220/35 ≈ 6.3×. Same battery size as the Q1 Max, and about 5–27 h more with the lights on.
